beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Orphan Gods makes vulnerable children responsible for other people's worlds.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their own survival depends on rewards they do not fully understand.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This science fiction novel begins after the adults abruptly disappear.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its children inhabit four dimensions, while human lives unfold within their tesses.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: They need guidance precisely when their power becomes most dangerous.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The premise connects abandonment with responsibility on an unsettling scale.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Following those children means asking what care becomes when suffering earns survival.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Iri loses familiar voices during an event called the Whitening.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Her surroundings become strange before any adult can explain the change.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The network that once carried parents and teachers falls silent.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A remaining system presents a number and an instruction to continue.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The opening makes that command frightening through a child's dependence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its unusual geometry belongs to a world she cannot fully understand.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin there, with loss and need, before treating the children as gods.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The children encounter human worlds through systems inherited from their absent adults.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their instruments make distant lives accessible without making them fully comprehensible.
